protocol.split: Batch A grouped corpus split (StratifiedGroupKFold, seed 0)
protocol.index: Batch A grouped dense index (train+val only)
protocol.fusion: alpha=0.4, same as deployed and Batch A
protocol.reference_definition: Distinct informative advisor answers logged on the test side of the query's question group. No reference is invented and no pool contains an index-side row.
protocol.reference_source: test side of the grouped split only
protocol.answer_text_policy: Answer text is not written to any result file; reports and artefacts carry ids, hashes and metrics only.
protocol.P1: unscreened grouped index (comparable with Batch A)

references_per_test_row.note: Row-weighted: rows inside very large near-duplicate groups pull the mean up.

skew.note: The reference distribution is highly skewed: a few very large transitive near-duplicate clusters hold hundreds of answers. Per-group and per-row statistics are reported separately.

reference_diversity.note: Pairwise token-F1 between reference answers in the same group. Low values mean the group holds genuinely different advice, not restatements of one answer.

reference_pools.summary_line: 11,747 distinct references in 4,457 test groups; 69.9% of test rows have >=2; mean max pairwise reference F1 0.6201; supports_multi_reference=True

checks.check: dense all test | own-reference token-F1 (informative gold)

reproduction_gate.note: Rankings are rebuilt from Batch A's own artefacts. If these do not match, the comparison is invalid and the run stops.

P1_sample | hybrid vs dense | max-other.comparison: P1_sample | hybrid vs dense | max-other | informative own answer only

non_informative_own_rows.note: On these rows the own logged 'answer' is a call-log note, not advice. The original metric still scores the retrieved answer against it, which is why single-reference F1 can exceed the informative-reference maximum on rows with one reference. This baseline is not an answer.

semantic_scale.note: Max semantic similarity grows with pool size because it is a maximum over more candidates; it is a wording-closeness statistic, not correctness and not a calibrated probability.

limitations: References are historical advisor answers, not verified-correct advice; agreement with them is not agricultural correctness.
Near-duplicate grouping is transitive at cosine >= 0.95, so some large groups may merge related but not identical questions.
Contradictory answers can coexist in one pool (Improvement 1 shows such conflicts exist); max-reference F1 rewards matching any of them.
Semantic similarity measures wording closeness only; it is not correctness and is reported separately from F1.
No human relevance or expert agronomic judgement exists for these pools (Batch B Phase 2 annotation remains PENDING).
Max-reference F1 and max semantic similarity both rise mechanically with pool size, because both are maxima over more candidates; the random-reference control is reported for that reason.

On rows whose own logged answer is a call-log note, the original single-reference metric scores against that note; those rows are reported separately and excluded from the informative-own paired comparison.
Only one grouped split seed was used, because the index rebuild is expensive; results are conditional on that split.
